609K Missouri’s most STUNNING dining view… Share this with someone who needs a dinner spot with a view 🌄 Follow @coupleofpatels for more bucket list travel inspo and hidden gems Can you believe this is in Missouri???🤯 This is Osage Restaurant📍 It’s located at Top of the Rock overlooking the breathtaking Table Rock Lake in the Ozark Mountains. 7,465 Here’s what you need to know ↓ I moved to Columbia, MO 16 years ago and grew up here. I graduated from the University of Missouri and then began my real estate career full time immediately after. I never thought I would stay here after college, but I realized I wasn’t ready to leave it behind. Columbia is a super unique town and I have a huge appreciation for this community. If you’re considering moving to Columbia, here’s what you need to know: -Columbia offers a blend of urban amenities and small-town charm, with vibrant local dining, shopping, and entertainment options. -The University of Missouri (Mizzou) is a major hub for culture, education, and sports events. -The real estate market is diverse, offering everything from historic homes to new construction in family-friendly neighborhoods. -Columbia is known for its beautiful parks and outdoor activities, including hiking and biking trails at the MKT Trail and Rock Bridge Memorial State Park. -The cost of living is relatively affordable compared to larger cities, with a lower-than-average housing market. -Columbia has a strong sense of community, with regular events, festivals, and a welcoming atmosphere for newcomers. If you live in Columbia, what would you add to the list?? -Olivia Taylor, Columbia, MO Realtor #columbiamo #mizzou #como #columbiamorealestate #columbiamorealtor

15.4K MIDWOOD SMOKEHOUSE – Keep this place in mind when the BBQ craving hits whether you live in Charlotte, Huntersville, Raleigh or the location I visited, Columbia. The restaurant has a menu packed with delicious appetizers (from queso to smoked meatballs), salads, sandwiches, BBQ plates, tacos, desserts, and something for my sip-sippers. There’s also private dining as well as full service catering. 📍702 Cross Hill Rd. Columbia, SC 📍Charlotte Locations: Ballantyne, Park Rd. The BBQ baked beans is worth checking out, but I prefer a more sweet taste to my baked beans than savory – MUST TRY.

## Please Be Considerate
Cracker Barrel provides a great restaurant and store with ample parking to accomodate RVs. Many even allow travellers to park and catch a few hours of rest (depending on city ordinances). Please use common courtesy and follow these guidelines to ensure that they will continue to extend this courtesy to us.
1.   Ask the store manager for permission to stay.  
2.   Do not stay for multiple days.  
3.   Leave it cleaner than you found it.  
4.   No grills, chairs, etc. Cracker Barrel is not a campground.  
5.   Buy something from the store or enjoy a delicious homestyle meal from the restaurant.

## Reviews
### “Not flat, HWY noise and low tree clearance ”
We've only been here an hour and the amount of motorcycle noise and loud muffler cars on the highway is significant. The lot on the smaller side and is not very flat either-it slopes down. The trees hang low and will hit the roof so be careful.
But there's not many other options-no WM that allows overnight RVs and apparantly the nearby Bass Pro doesn't either.
There was a Loves with RV parking-dedicated sites away from the truckers (some even pull thru) with electric and water (plus access to the dump site but no sewage hook up) about 30 mins west, reserve a spot on the app, it might be better than here.
Was this review helpful?

## Reviews
### “Great for small rigs”
We ordered to go dinner 35 minutes from arrival, and they had it ready for us when we pulled in. There are only 8 RV spots, perfect for smaller rigs (about 40-45’ in length). The area felt safe, and our children enjoyed front porch checkers before heading to bed. There is also a Burger King adjacent to the parking lot with the drive through open 5 am to midnight (but restrooms were closed after 9 when the dining room closed). The QT gas station across the street and on the right by the interstate was easy to pull through for one last fill up before continuing our journey.

Heading out west and this is the second time staying at this Cracker Barrel in our truck camper. Love the convenience of dinner and breakfast when making miles per day. Other than that there were no issues. The RV bus parking area is behind the restaurant so the noise from the highway is less than you would usually have.

### “Best spot for an overnight stay”
Heading out west and this is the second time staying at this Cracker Barrel in our truck camper. Love the convenience of dinner and breakfast when making miles per day. I always call in case policy changes but so far all Cracker Barrel’s that I’ve called have always allowed overnight camping. Even has grass to walk dogs. I just wish EVERYONE would clean up after their dogs.

### “Cracker Barrel”
The people that we spoke to on the phone were friendly, inviting and informative about why they have overnighters. Breakfast not included (laugh here) but the food was good. We were thankful to have this location.

### “Its a Cracker Barrel seen one seen them all”
We enjoyed the night stay here but at 10 p.m. when the restaurant closed, a truck pulled up with a portable power washer and for the next hour and a half they power washed the trash area which we were parked  right next to.  Other than that there were no issues. The RV bus parking area is behind the restaurant so the noise from the highway is less than you would usually have.
